spec.notes: designed after REAL-01 (2026-07-30 cut) showed a market-wide drift; registered before any exploratory peer-relative look at the REAL-01 data; tests the method on account series, not the product thresholds
spec.outcome: y_i = post-window drift of account i > median post-window drift of the evaluated accounts (accounts eligible pre and with >= 14 post-window days; Hyperliquid also >= 1 interval, OKX >= 30 daily returns)
spec.outcome_data: a new package with the same structure (same Hyperliquid sample addresses, same OKX lead traders), data up to at least 2027-01-30, integrity checked with its MANIFESTs; same parsers

prediction_data.note: already opened for REAL-01; only data up to the cut 2026-10-30 is used here, and the outcomes (after the cut) did not exist when this was registered

spec.question: Prospective: is the NPMLE predictive probability that an account's drift beats the median of its peers over 2026-10-30 to 2027-01-30 calibrated, better than chance, and at least as good as the t-stat?
spec.relative_drift: x_i = realdata.drift(pre-window intervals).mu minus the median of x over the dataset's eligible accounts; se_i from the same fit
spec.success: hyperliquid, all of: (1) ECE <= max(0.05, ece_noise95) AND (2) AUC(P_beat) - 0.5 lower 95 % bound > 0 AND (3) AUC(P_beat) - AUC(t_rel) lower 95 % bound >= -0.01

payload.finding: peer-relative version of REAL-01 on the already opened package (pre 2026-01-30..07-30, post 07-30..10-30), run AFTER REAL-02 was registered and its predictions frozen, so it cannot have shaped REAL-02

spec.accounts_and_eligibility: as REAL-02 (Hyperliquid sample minus first address, >= 10 intervals over >= 60 days in the pre window; OKX leads minus first trader, >= 60 days)
spec.data: as REAL-02 (predictions from realdata_2026-10-30, zip sha256 0b851ea48bb28a2b887ed20e8f7154fef88a43576756e5437c57ef7a6c2240ff, data up to the cut only; outcomes from a new package with data to >= 2027-01-30, MANIFESTs checked)
spec.evaluation_procedure: as REAL-02: registered commit, recompute predictions, verify sha256, then outcomes
spec.frozen_predictions: sha256 of canonical JSON {dataset: {id: [p_corr, t_rel]}} stored in the registry by --predict
spec.notes: hypotheses come from an exploratory look at already-opened data (registry note 'REAL-02 exploratory'); only the prospective outcomes can confirm them
spec.outcome: y_i = post-window drift > median post-window drift of the evaluated accounts (outcome rules as REAL-02)
spec.question: Prospective: do the accounts with the lowest relative t-stat keep lagging the median of their peers over 2026-10-30 to 2027-01-30? Secondary: calibration of a median-corrected NPMLE probability; OKX reversal

scores.p_corr: NPMLE posterior of x_i = mu_i - median mu (skill.npmle_summary, thr 0); P_i(m) = sum_g post_ig Phi((g - m) / se_f_i), se_f_i = sigma_i / sqrt(92); m = the value making mean_i P_i(m) = 0.5 (median of the model's own predictive distribution; bisection); p_corr = P_i(m)
scores.t_rel: (mu_i - median mu) / se_i from realdata.drift over the pre window

secondary.auc: AUC of p_corr and of t_rel
secondary.bottom_decile_okx: share y, bottom decile of t_rel
secondary.calibration: ECE of p_corr vs ece_noise95 (as REAL-01)
secondary.top_decile: share y among the top decile of t_rel (hyperliquid and okx); okx hypothesis from the exploration: below 0.5 (reversal)

spec.success: hyperliquid: among the bottom decile of t_rel (evaluated accounts), share with y = 1 has an upper 95 % bootstrap bound (2000 resamples of accounts, rng seed 0) <= 0.30
